note: h at column 1 must fail, not wrap to the previous line
l stops on the last character in normal mode
2$ goes to the end of the NEXT line
the remembered column must survive a short line in between
after $ the cursor stays at end of each line, however long
{n}G lands on the first non-blank of line n
same cursor_down() rule as j/dd: fails ONLY from the last line, clamps to it otherwise — found by fuzzing an engine that beeped on every overshoot instead of just the boundary one
a run of punctuation counts as its own word for w, but not for W
an empty line is itself a word
e already at a word end must advance to the NEXT word end
Starting ON a blank must not strip the word behind it — the word class is taken at the original cursor, before the first backward step.
a word/punct boundary is a word END — ge from 'c' lands on '-'
The virtual end-of-line position terminates word runs, so ge from 'a' of "bar" must stop at the END of "foo", not merge the two words.
; after t must advance rather than stick in place
% jumps from the first bracket at or after the cursor
x with too large a count deletes to end of line, it does not fail
deleting the only character leaves an empty line and clamps the cursor
r never does a partial replace
replacing a character with itself changes nothing, yet r ran, so it mints an undo block for the u to burn on — the x survives.
u as the very first key must do nothing — undo history starts empty

Listed as groups so each x is its own undo block. Fed as one string, feedkeys collapses all three deletions into a single block and one u would restore everything — which is not what interactive Vim does.
0 is the line-start motion, never a count digit
the black hole must not clobber the unnamed register
